hard_gate_idle_lifecycle.question: Does Pinecone Starter suspend, archive, or delete indexes after inactivity, in a way comparable to Zilliz Free's auto-suspend?

basis.fact: The only documented automatic data-deletion triggers are: (1) user-initiated deletion (soft-deleted, retained up to 90 days), (2) non-payment account deactivation (data retained 30 days before permanent deletion), (3) full account/service closure. Mere inactivity is not among them.

No inactivity/pause/suspend/archive clause found in any current lifecycle-relevant doc checked: reference/quotas-and-limits, reference/api/database-limits, reference/quotas-and-rate-limits, guides/manage-cost/understanding-cost, guides/manage-data/manage-indexes, guides/organizations/manage-billing/manage-your-billing-plan, guides/production/data-deletion, pinecone.io/pricing.
basis.classification: DERIVED (absence-of-evidence across an exhaustive, named page set, not a single positive citation)

historical_context_important.note: Pinecone's OLD pod-based free tier DID have an inactivity policy. This is the likely source of confusion with stale blog posts and forum threads, and is recorded here precisely so it is not mistaken for current behavior.

timeline.event: Official blog states inactive indexes on the free plan 'will be archived after 7 days of inactivity' (1 day for ephemeral/Auto-GPT-style indexes); archived indexes became collections, recreatable 'within a few minutes'.
Official blog: Pinecone REMOVED this policy - 'No more auto-archiving of inactive indexes,' allowing free indexes to be kept indefinitely.

timeline.note: No evidence found that the policy was ever reinstated. Today's Starter plan is serverless-only; the old pod-based gcp-starter tier is legacy, with a dedicated migration doc confirming the architecture change (idle serverless compute isn't billed/reclaimed the way pod-based always-on compute was, which is plausibly why the old policy doesn't carry over).

unverified_claims_explicitly_debunked.claim: "Indexes on the Starter plan are paused after 3 weeks of inactivity" - repeated by several SEO/review sites (layer3labs.io, costbench.com, ranksquire.com, pecollective.com) and surfaced by search-engine synthesis as if factual.
unverified_claims_explicitly_debunked.finding: Could not be traced to any primary source. The specific review pages a search engine cited as the origin were fetched directly and neither actually contains the claim - it appears to be an artifact of search-tool synthesis, not a real citation.
unverified_claims_explicitly_debunked.classification: INFERENCE (specifically: identified and rejected as unsupported)
unverified_claims_explicitly_debunked.separately: A 2022 Pinecone Community thread has a staff reply claiming indexes were 'deleted after 7 days of inactivity' - but this predates serverless entirely (pod-based only) and predates even the 2023 policy history above, so it is obsolete and not current-state evidence.

ondemand_clarification.finding: "OnDemand" in current Pinecone docs is a read-capacity BILLING mode for serverless indexes (pay-per-read-unit, the default), contrasted with paid "Dedicated" (always-warm Dedicated Read Nodes) - it is not a cluster-suspend/resume mechanism. No documented 'index sleeps, then a control-plane resume takes N minutes' pattern (the Zilliz-style behavior) was found anywhere.
ondemand_clarification.nuance: A real but much smaller effect exists: per-namespace query-path caching. 'Warm namespaces' (queried regularly, cached locally) get lower latency; 'cold-start queries' to an infrequently-accessed namespace have higher latency. No documented numeric cold-start duration was found. Pinecone's Dedicated Read Nodes product page frames itself as eliminating 'cold start latency regressions' that OnDemand can exhibit for cold namespaces - the closest official acknowledgment that OnDemand has some latency variability, but this is a per-query-path effect, not an outage/resume event, and nothing suggests multi-minute magnitude.
ondemand_clarification.classification: OFFICIAL_VENDOR_FACT (existence of the effect) + explicit absence of a duration figure (not fabricated)
ondemand_clarification.implication_for_benchmarking: The 2026-08-15 mandate's idle/cold-query benchmark requirement (distinguishing warm vs. first-query-after-idle vs. subsequent-warm) is still worth executing empirically even though no vendor-documented duration exists - see task #38.
